content: The text provided is a list of references, primarily related to breastfeeding, maternal and child health, and associated healthcare practices. 1. UNICEF provides data on monitoring the health and well-being of children and women, accessible at their official website as of March 7, 2018. 2. A joint statement by WHO and UNICEF emphasizes the importance of protecting, promoting, and supporting breastfeeding, particularly through maternity services. This document was accessed on March 7, 2018. 3. The Innocenti Declaration outlines the global commitment to the protection, promotion, and support of breastfeeding. This declaration was accessed on September 7, 2018. 4. The International Code of Marketing of Breast-Milk Substitutes, a critical document for regulating the marketing of formula products, was accessed on March 7, 2018. 5. The 2017 update to the International Code of Marketing of Breast-Milk Substitutes includes frequently asked questions and was accessed on March 7, 2018. 6. WHO provides resolutions and guidelines on nutrition, including the Ten Steps to Successful Breastfeeding, which was accessed on March 7, 2018. 7. The 47th World Health Assembly in 1994 addressed infant and young child nutrition, with resolutions and decisions available online as of March 7, 2018. 8. The 49th World Health Assembly in 1996 also focused on infant and young child nutrition, with relevant documents accessed on March 7, 2018. 9. The Innocenti Declaration of 2005, presented in Florence, Italy, reaffirmed global efforts to improve infant and young child feeding practices. This document was accessed on March 7, 2018. 10. The Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI) has been revised and expanded to integrate care for mothers and newborns. The updated guidelines were accessed on March 7, 2018. 11. WHO's comprehensive implementation plan on maternal, infant, and young child nutrition, presented at the 65th World Health Assembly in 2012, was accessed on March 7, 2018. 12. WHO's Global Nutrition Targets for 2025 outline key objectives for improving maternal and child nutrition. These targets were accessed on March 7, 2018. 13. The Second International Conference on Nutrition, held in Rome in 2014, produced a framework for action to address global nutrition challenges. This document was accessed on March 7, 2018. 14. The United Nations Decade of Action on Nutrition (2016–2025) includes frequently asked questions and was accessed on March 7, 2018. 15. Decision WHA68(14) from the 68th World Health Assembly in 2015 focuses on developing core indicators for maternal, infant, and young child nutrition. This decision was accessed on March 7, 2018. 16. Indicators for the Global Monitoring Framework on maternal, infant, and young child nutrition were accessed on March 7, 2018. 17. Labook MH discusses global monitoring data for the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative in a 2012 publication in Breastfeeding Medicine. 18. National implementation data for the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative was accessed on March 7, 2018. 19. The PROBIT trial, a randomized breastfeeding intervention trial conducted in Belarus, was published in JAMA in 2001. 20. Pérez-Escamilla et al. conducted a systematic review on the impact of the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative on breastfeeding and child health outcomes, published in Maternal and Child Nutrition in 2016. 21. DiGirolamo et al. examined the effects of maternity-care practices on breastfeeding in a 2008 Pediatrics supplement. 22. Saadeh RJ reviewed the progress and future directions of the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative after 20 years in a 2012 publication in the Journal of Human Lactation. 23. Munn et al. analyzed the impact of the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative in the United States on early infant health and breastfeeding outcomes, published in Breastfeeding Medicine in 2016. 24. UNICEF and WHO compiled case studies on the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative from various countries, accessed on March 7, 2018. 25. The Pan American Health Organization and WHO Regional Office for the Americas reviewed the status, challenges, and opportunities of the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative in Latin America and the Caribbean, accessed on March 7, 2018. 26. WHO's handbook for guideline development, 2nd edition, published in 2014, was accessed on March 7, 2018. 27. The revised Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative of 2018 was developed by WHO and UNICEF, with details from the 2016 BFHI Congress accessed on March 7, 2018. 28. Nyqvist et al. introduced the Neo-BFHI, an adaptation of the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative for neonatal wards, with guiding principles and ten steps to support breastfeeding, accessed on March 7, 2018. 29. Jaafar et al. reviewed the effects of restricted pacifier use on breastfeeding duration in term infants, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016. 30. Foster et al. examined non-nutritive sucking for improving physiological stability and nutrition in preterm infants, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016. 31. Greene et al. reviewed oral stimulation techniques to promote oral feeding in preterm infants, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016. 32. WHO's guidance on ending inappropriate promotion of foods for infants and young children was presented at the 69th World Health Assembly in 2016. 33. WHO and UNICEF updated guidelines on HIV and infant feeding, focusing on breastfeeding duration and health service support for mothers living with HIV, accessed on March 7, 2018. 34. WHO's framework on integrated, people-centered health services was presented at the 69th World Health Assembly in 2016. 35. Smith and Kroeger explored the impact of birthing practices on breastfeeding in the second edition of their book, published in 2010. 36. WHO's 2015 publication addresses the prevention and elimination of disrespect and abuse during facility-based childbirth. 37. Piwoz and Huffman analyzed the impact of breast-milk substitute marketing on WHO-recommended breastfeeding practices in a 2015 Food and Nutrition Bulletin article. 38. The International Baby Food Action Network documented violations of the International Code of Marketing of Breast-Milk Substitutes from 2011 to 2013 in a 2014 report. 39. Baker et al. examined global trends in commercial milk-based formula sales and their implications for infant and young child feeding in a 2016 Public Health Nutrition article. 40. The 39th World Health Assembly in 1986 addressed infant and young child feeding, with resolutions and decisions accessed on March 7, 2018. 41. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services provides information on risk factors for preterm labor and birth, accessed on March 7, 2018. 42. Stevens et al. reviewed the benefits of immediate or early skin-to-skin contact after cesarean delivery in a 2014 Maternal and Child Nutrition article. 43. The implications of cesarean delivery for breastfeeding outcomes and strategies to support breastfeeding were discussed in a 2014 technical brief by Alive & Thrive. 44. WHO's practical guide on kangaroo mother care was accessed on March 7, 2018. 45. Nyqvist et al. studied the development of breastfeeding behavior in preterm infants in a 1999 Early Human Development article. 46. McFadden et al. reviewed support strategies for breastfeeding mothers with healthy term babies in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2017. 47. Meier et al. discussed lactation risks for late preterm infants and their mothers in a 2007 Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health article. 48. Becker et al. reviewed methods of milk expression for lactating women in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016. 49. Salvatori and Guaraldi examined the effects of breast and formula feeding on gut microbiota development in newborns in a 2012 Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology article. 50. WHO and UNICEF outlined acceptable medical reasons for using breast-milk substitutes in a 2009 publication. 51. Kellams et al. updated the ABM Clinical Protocol on supplementary feedings in healthy term breastfed neonates in a 2017 Breastfeeding Medicine article. 52. WHO and FAO published guidelines on the safe preparation, storage, and handling of powdered infant formula in 2007. 53. DeMarchis et al. proposed an integrated human milk banking approach to strengthen newborn care in a 2017 Journal of Perinatology article. 54. Bu’Lock et al. studied the coordination of sucking, swallowing, and breathing in term and preterm infants in a 1990 Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology article. 55. Woolridge discussed challenges in establishing lactation in a 1996 Food and Nutrition Bulletin article. 56. WHO's coaching manual for improving hospital care quality for mothers and newborns was accessed on March 7, 2018. 57. WHO's learner manual for improving hospital care quality for mothers and newborns was published in 2017. 58. The Institute for Healthcare Improvement provides resources on quality improvement in healthcare, accessed on March 7, 2018. 59. The Breakthrough Series by the Institute for Healthcare Improvement outlines a collaborative model for achieving significant improvements in healthcare. 60. The DHS Program offers a model questionnaire for demographic and health surveys, accessed on March 7, 2018. 61. UNICEF, WHO, and other organizations advocate for breastfeeding as a critical investment in national health and wealth, accessed on March 7, 2018. 62. Sinha et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of interventions to improve breastfeeding outcomes, published in Acta Paediatrica in 2015. 63. UNICEF provides additional resources on maternal and child health, accessed on March 7, 2018.
